title: Add staged controlplane subnet rollout with DNS-stamp and peering guardrails
text:
Add staged controlplane subnet rollout with DNS-stamp and peering guardrails

description:
Motivation: customers running Private control planes across large VPCs asked for a safer, automatable way to expand or migrate controlplane subnets across AZ boundaries while preserving DNS ownership and peering safety. This PR introduces a staged rollout pattern for controlplane subnets that combines: 1) a lightweight DNS-stamp mechanism (a stamped TXT/alias that signals DNS precedence and readiness), 2) canary subnet labels and selectors to limit initial traffic, and 3) explicit peering acceptance guardrails to avoid accidental route churn.

What this changes (single-line summary): additions to the controlplane subnet Terraform module (dns_stamp resource, staged_rollout boolean, canary_label), a rollout orchestration Terraform file and a helper script (upgrade_safe_rollout.sh) which runs preflight checks, performs incremental subnet handoffs, validates DNS-stamp propagation, and can rollback partial changes. Helm chart values are wired so installer operators can toggle canary selectors per-deployment. Integration tests and docs added.

Implementation notes: the dns_stamp concept is intentionally conservative: we create a short-lived Route53 TXT record + optional ALIAS pointing to the new controlplane target that acts as a marker for health probes and for downstream resolvers to prefer the new prefix only after stamp validation. The module exposes stamp_ttl and stamp_health_check variables so operators can tune propagation windows. The staged_rollout flow supports two phases: CANARY (0-10% traffic, limited by subnet selectors and SG scoping) and SWEEP (full migration). Peering guardrails add an explicit accept_with_token step (requires the remote account to approve a token, preventing accidental broad accept).

Checklist (manual steps and automation covered):
- [x] Terraform module changes (backwards compatible defaults)
- [x] Add dns_stamp and stamp validation plan in integration tests
- [x] Add rollout orchestration script with idempotent operations and safe rollback
- [x] Expose helm toggles for canary selectors and stamp-enabled mode
- [x] Document runbook and failure modes + alerts to watch

Health checks and CI: unit terraform plan tests and an integration test that spins a mocked Route53 zone were added. CI was initially flaky for the integration test due to a mock timeout; increased retries and the pipeline now passes (see ci/status).

Security and backwards compatibility: defaults keep staged_rollout disabled; dns_stamp resources are opt-in. SG changes are scoped and use named security-group fragments so existing policies should remain functional. No secrets are added; peering token is ephemeral and logged only at debug level.

Rollout guidance (operator):
1) Toggle staged_rollout=true in terraform for the target workspace. 2) Run terraform apply which creates canary subnets and dns_stamp in a paused state. 3) Run installer/scripts/upgrade_safe_rollout.sh --canary to perform canary handoff; validate endpoints and DNS-stamp propagation. 4) If canary looks good, run --sweep to complete migration. 5) Use --rollback to revert to previous state; the script performs reversal of peering acceptances and removes stamps.

Related: ENG-4823 (staged rollout design), INFRA-921 (Route53 staging behavior).

Notes for reviewers: focus on the rollback idempotency of upgrade_safe_rollout.sh and the peering token acceptance flow in terraform/modules/peering. I included a small test harness in tests/integration/test_staged_rollout.py that simulates stamp propagation delays.

Merge outcome: squash-merged to main after addressing review feedback.


review_comments:
Jonas Meyer: Left a couple of nit comments on the script logging and suggested we emit a structured event when a stamp transitions to 'validated' so downstream watchers can subscribe. Also questioned whether TXT vs ALIAS is correct tradeoff in cross-account setups.
Marisol Vega (author): Replied that the text stamp is the lowest risk; ALIAS is optional and gated behind a variable. Added a structured CloudWatch metric emit in the script per Jonas' suggestion.
Priya Nair: Asked for an explicit test around SG scoping when canary and sweep subnets co-exist. Added tests/integration/test_staged_rollout.py to cover this scenario.
Derek Huang: Requested a small doc section on how Route53 resolver caching can delay stamp visibility; I expanded docs/runbooks/controlplane-rollout.md with troubleshooting steps and TTL recommendations.
CI bot: initial integration run failed due to mock Route53 timeout; re-run after increasing retry backoff, all checks passed.
